claims.text: Abscess is a clinical diagnosis; send Gram stain and culture mainly to find MRSA and get susceptibilities.
claims.quote: Gram stain and culture are generally recommended, primarily to identify MRSA and obtain antimicrobial susceptibility testing

claims.text: Point-of-care ultrasound when it is unclear whether there is an abscess or only cellulitis.
claims.quote: Point-of-care ultrasound can improve diagnostic accuracy and help distinguish an abscess from cellulitis when there is diagnostic uncertainty

claims.text: Ruptured epidermal cysts are often cultured but rarely grow pathogens: the inflammation is a reaction to keratin.
claims.quote: Although ruptured epidermal cysts mimic abscesses and are often cultured, they rarely reveal pathogens because the inflammation is typically a foreign body reaction to keratin rather than a true bacterial infection.

claims.text: Perineal abscess: consider a deeper perirectal abscess or a Crohn disease fistula.
claims.quote: Perineal abscesses may represent cutaneous emergence of a deeper perirectal abscess or drainage resulting from Crohn disease via a fistulous tract.
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Cutaneous Abscess, Differential diagnosis
